inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average, Q2 2026 10-Q (389.5m; basic 388.4m at 30 Jun 2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks paused for 2026 after Boyd Thermal, so the flat count is a modelling convention for FY2026 that the company funded in FY2024-25 (US$2.5bn and US$1.9bn repurchased).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 10-Q: long-term debt 18,520 + current portion 11 + short-term borrowings (commercial paper) 2,091 = 20,622 total debt; cash 483 + short-term investments 212 = 695. The Metrics CSV total_debt (18,531) omits the 2,091 of commercial paper drawn to fund Boyd Thermal. Operating lease liabilities (~US$0.8bn) excluded: under US GAAP the lease cost is already inside operating expense and OCF.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 14 (Equity-Based Compensation): pre-tax expense for stock options 20 + RSUs/RSAs 84 + PSUs 22 = 126; plus 52 of cash paid for tax withholding on net-share settlement (financing activities, XBRL PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation). Eaton publishes no combined figure so the two lines are summed. History (SBC / withholding): FY2020 92/37, FY2021 101/47, FY2022 97/60, FY2023 97/49, FY2024 108/70, FY2025 126/52. Note 14 also shows FY2025 vest-date fair value (RSU 107 + PSU ~60 + option intrinsic 88 = ~255) well above the grant-date expense, so 178 is if anything light; immaterial at <1% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases US$1,862m (FY2024 2,492m). Zero in H1 2026; management paused 2026 buybacks after the US$9.55bn Boyd Thermal acquisition. US$9.0bn authorisation outstanding but unspent.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated Monday 2026-09-28 before the open
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf ~4.2% (10y UST, Sep 2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 (large-cap electrical/industrial) -> cost of equity ~9.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (2025-26 note issues for Boyd/Ultra PCS), ~4.0% after tax. Weights: equity ~US$171bn market cap (89%) / debt US$20.6bn (11%) -> WACC ~9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and data-centre concentration are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842): operating lease cost (US$251m FY2025) is inside cost of sales/SG&A and the US$198m of payments is inside OCF, so EBITDA and FCF are already after leases. Lease liabilities therefore excluded from net debt; no lease_cost_pct_path. Finance leases negligible (US$9m principal).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests US$45m at 30 Jun 2026 (net income to NCI US$3m FY2025) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, industrial/cyclical). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Owner FCF = reported FCF 3,553 - SBC incl. withholding 178 - interest income 0 = 3,375 (FY2025). Interest income not stripped: Eaton is a net borrower (net debt ~US$19.9bn, 5.9x owner FCF) and reports only 'Interest expense - net'. Consolidated flows INCLUDE the Vehicle + eMobility (Mobility Group, ~18% of revenue) through the whole horizon even though the Dana Reverse Morris Trust is expected to close by end-Q1 2027: at close today's Eaton holders receive >=50.1% of the combined Dana entity in kind plus Eaton keeps a ~US$1.1bn cash distribution, so the Mobility value stays with the present shareholder either way and is not double-counted; the US$250m targeted synergies and any Dana re-rating are upside not in the model, and the post-separation margin uplift is deliberately not taken because the revenue is also not removed. 10-year horizon because growth is decelerating from ~20% and the margin path is still ramping at year 5. D&A path converges on the capex path by year 10 so the ~US$500m/yr of acquired-intangible amortisation tax shield is not perpetuated in the terminal value. FY2026 (year 1) revenue = organic 11-13% guided (Q2 2026) + ~6pp from Boyd Thermal (closed 12 Mar 2026), Ultra PCS (23 Jan 2026), Fibrebond and Resilient Power -> ~19.5%; H1 2026 was +19.2% and Q3 guide is 13.5-15.5% organic. Year-1 EBITDA margin 23.0% is GAAP-ish: H1 2026 GAAP EBITDA pre-SBC was ~20.5% with Boyd inventory step-up, deal and separation costs, versus FY2025 adjusted (ex-amortisation, ex-M&A charges) ~23.8% pre-SBC; for a serial acquirer the M&A and restructuring charges recur, so the base path only reaches 24.5%.

equity_bridge.note: 30 Jun 2026 10-Q balance sheet; consolidated flows so deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.5%/5.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (9.8%/9.0%) and EPS (19.3%/24.5%): Eaton returns most of its earnings as dividends (US$1.6bn FY2025) and buybacks (US$1.9bn), so book value is not a growth anchor; revenue CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2022->FY2025 (3y) and FY2020->FY2025 (5y). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC incl. withholding): FY2020 2,426; FY2021 1,440; FY2022 1,778; FY2023 2,721; FY2024 3,341; FY2025 3,375. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within ~1pp because SBC is <1% of revenue. The 5-year figures are depressed by the FY2020 COVID trough and the 2021 Hydraulics (Danfoss) and Lighting divestitures; FY2021 OCF was also hit by working-capital rebuild. The 3-year EPS/FCF CAGRs (19-24%) reflect the data-centre-driven margin expansion from 2023 and are not a run-rate.

base.growth_note: FY2026 = guided 11-13% organic + ~6pp acquired (Boyd Thermal 9.5 months, Ultra PCS, Fibrebond, Resilient) + ~1pp FX. FY2027-28 hold high-single/low-double digit on the data-centre backlog (only ~20% converts near term, majority 2028+) plus a residual 2 months of Boyd. Decelerates to 3.5% by year 10.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA. FY2025 GAAP 22.9%, FY2025 adjusted (ex intangible amortisation and M&A charges) ~23.8%. Year 1 at 23.0% carries Boyd step-up/deal/separation costs; matures at 24.5% on Electrical mix and Boyd/Fibrebond synergies.
base.da_capex_note: FY2025 D&A 1,006 (3.7%) = depreciation 477 + amortisation 486 + other; FY2026 ~4.4% with Boyd/Ultra intangibles (H1 2026 D&A 671). Capex 3.3% FY2025, 3.5% while data-centre capacity is built out. D&A glides to the 3.4% capex rate so the terminal value carries no perpetual amortisation shield.
base.tax_note: Cash taxes paid / EBIT: FY2023 18.3%, FY2024 16.0%, FY2025 17.6%; Irish-domiciled, adjusted ETR guided ~17%. Ramps to 19% for Pillar Two / mix.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables (net trade WC ~20% of revenue), partly offset by growing customer advances (deferred revenue 602 -> 1,133 over 18 months on data-centre orders). FY2023-25 OCF absorbed 25-30% of each year's revenue increase in WC and other; -15% net of advances.

bull.narrative: AI/hyperscale capex keeps compounding through 2029: Electrical Americas data-centre revenue (+65% YoY in Q2 2026) converts the 15-year backlog faster than the ~20% near-term rate management cites; Boyd Thermal liquid cooling wins the GPU-generation transitions against Vertiv and the chip-to-grid bundle lifts content per site; Aerospace aftermarket and Ultra PCS defence content hold 23%+ segment margins; the Dana RMT closes on time and the US$250m synergies re-rate the retained stake. Margin reaches 26.5% pre-SBC on Electrical mix; customer advances keep WC drag to -12%.

bear.narrative: Hyperscale capex digestion in 2027-28: data-centre orders roll over after the 2026 peak, backlog conversion slips as customers re-phase sites, and the capacity Eaton is adding ahead of demand runs under-absorbed. Boyd Thermal (bought at 22.5x EBITDA) sees GPU-cooling architectures shift and pricing pressure from Vertiv; step-up and integration costs run longer. Tariffs and copper are only partly passed through. The Dana RMT slips or closes with a lower retained-stake value; buybacks stay paused while US$20bn of acquisition debt is worked down. Revenue flat in 2028, margin troughs at 20.5% pre-SBC, WC absorbs more as advances unwind; terminal capped at 18x for a cyclical.

scenario_narratives.base: Eaton executes its 2026 guide (11-13% organic, adjusted EPS US$13.40-13.60) and the acquired businesses annualise, taking FY2026 revenue to ~US$32.8bn. Data-centre backlog converts steadily rather than in a rush, so growth steps down from ~20% to high-single digits by 2028 and to GDP-plus by year 10. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers from the deal-cost-laden 23.0% to 24.5% as Electrical mix and Boyd/Fibrebond synergies come through, but not further, because acquisition and restructuring charges recur for a serial acquirer. Capex stays at 3.5% while capacity is built, then 3.4%. The Mobility Group remains in the consolidated flows; the Dana RMT is treated as an in-kind distribution that neither adds nor removes value for today's holder.
scenario_narratives.bull: See assumptions.bull.narrative: sustained AI capex through 2029, faster backlog conversion, Boyd wins the thermal transitions, margin to 26.5%, RMT synergies realised.
scenario_narratives.bear: See assumptions.bear.narrative: 2027-28 hyperscale digestion, under-absorbed capacity, Boyd multiple not earned, RMT slips, margin troughs at 20.5%, cyclical 18x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear up: an unusually large share of both the growth and the multiple now rests on one end market (hyperscale data-centre capex) whose 2027-28 path is genuinely uncertain, US$11bn was spent on acquisitions in Q1 2026 alone with Boyd at 22.5x EBITDA, net debt is ~5.9x owner FCF and buybacks are paused -- but there is no solvency or covenant risk, so not 35%. Bull down: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once (AI capex continuing, Boyd thermal share, four simultaneous integrations, the Dana RMT closing on time and re-rating), which the method says warrants a lower bull weight.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF DCF on consolidated Eaton, SBC expensed (immaterial here at ~0.65% of revenue), interest income not stripped because the company is a large net borrower, 9% USD WACC held constant across scenarios with risk carried in the flows and the weights. The key finding is the gap between what the flows support and what the price pays: at ~US$440 the market is capitalising owner FCF of ~US$3.4bn (FY2025) at ~55x EV/FCF and ~44x trailing earnings, which a 10-year explicit build with 20% first-year growth and a Gordon terminal at 9%/3% cannot reach without assuming either a sub-7% discount rate or a terminal multiple above the 20x cap. The valuation should be read as 'what does the price already assume', and the required-return table is the more useful output than the point estimate. The pending Mobility/Dana Reverse Morris Trust (expected close by end-Q1 2027) is deliberately left inside the consolidated flows: it is a distribution in kind (>=50.1% of combined Dana to Eaton holders plus ~US$1.1bn cash to Eaton), so it moves value between pockets rather than creating or destroying it for the present shareholder; after it closes this model should be rebuilt on a continuing-operations (Electrical + Aerospace) base with the retained Dana stake and the cash in the equity bridge, and the pure-play margin uplift taken only then.
key_risks_to_valuation: Data-centre capex cycle: the fastest-growing ~15-20% of revenue and most of the multiple depend on hyperscale/colocation spending continuing; a 2027-28 digestion is the bear case and is weighted 25%
Acquisition returns: US$11bn deployed in Q1 2026 (Boyd Thermal ~22.5x EBITDA, Ultra PCS) at low first-year cash returns; net debt ~US$19.9bn, buybacks paused

Terminal assumptions dominate: with 20% year-1 growth decelerating over 10 years, most of the value sits in the terminal; each 1pp of WACC or 0.5pp of terminal growth moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid)
Mobility/Dana RMT: regulatory and shareholder approvals through Q1 2027; the model neither credits the US$250m synergies nor charges separation dis-synergies or stranded corporate cost
Margin path assumes M&A and restructuring charges (~1pp of revenue in FY2025) continue; the street's adjusted-EPS basis excludes them and reads ~1pp higher
Tariffs, copper and component inflation are only partly passed through; Pillar Two could lift the ~17% Irish-domiciled tax rate faster than the 19% terminal assumed
